subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity & SLA targets (Acme Health)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood-inference.com>
To: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@acmehealth.com>, Priya Menon <priya.m@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood-inference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity & SLA targets (Acme Health)

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Production inference latency spikes during morning batch loads (p99 ~650ms) impacting clinician workflows.
- Strict data isolation requirements (PHI) — cannot use multi-tenant hosted instances.
- Need predictable per-hour throughput for batch and peak interactive API traffic (+ ability to burst for seasonal campaigns).
- Goal: move to Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) with SLA for latency/availability and private networking (VPC).

Proposed dedicated configuration (high-level)
- Reserved pool: 8x A100 80GB equivalent (NVIDIA A100-80GB) with single-tenant isolation.
- Scaling plan: baseline 8 GPUs, auto-burst to +4 GPUs for daily peak windows via reserved burst capacity.
- KV-caching + prefix caching to reduce token cost for repeated queries (expected ~30% token reduction).
- Target SLOs: 99.9% availability, p95 latency <=180ms, p99 latency <=400ms for interactive routes.

Security & compliance notes
- Private control plane + VPC peering, customer-managed KMS for key material.
- We will supply SOC 2 Type II artifacts and an environment diagram; Dev will coordinate the security questionnaire.

Attachments included
- Dedicated_Capacity_Proposal_AcmeHealth_v2.pdf (configuration, pricing bands, timeline)
- SOW_Draft_AcmeHealth.docx (SOW template for review)

Next steps & Owners
1) Acme: confirm the baseline GPU count and whether the proposed p99/p95 SLOs match SLAs you want to target (Sam) — by Tue 6/23.
2) Redwood: share a redline-friendly SOW and updated pricing (Marissa) — sent herewith.
3) Security: Dev to send SOC 2 artifacts and questionnaire answers (Dev) — by 6/24.
4) Procurement: once SOW/pricing aligned, we’ll route DocuSign and your procurement team can sign (Procurement).

If that looks right, I’ll schedule a short call early next week with Dev to walk through the security appendix and the ramp plan.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood-inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity & SLA targets (Acme Health)

Thanks Marissa — very helpful summary. A few clarifying points from our side:

1) Baseline GPUs: we are leaning toward 12 x A100-80GB rather than 8 based on current growth forecasts (expected 40% QoQ). Can you re-run the cost with 12 baseline + burst +4?
2) SLO targets: p95 <=180ms is fine; p99 target of <=400ms is aggressive but acceptable for interactive routes if we have guaranteed isolation. Can you confirm what happens if p99 slips during organic traffic spikes — are there automatic fallbacks to a slightly larger model or region?
3) Security: we need the network topology diagram and an export of audit log retention policy for 12 months (minimum). Priya will own the security review.

Procurement is looped for timing — our target is to have procurement sign off in the first week of July.

Sam Ortiz
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Health
sam.ortiz@acmehealth.com

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity & SLA targets (Acme Health)

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Sam — notes inline below and attached an updated pricing appendix.

1) Baseline GPUs: will re-price for 12x baseline + burst +4. Ballpark: +50% on monthly reserved fee vs the 8x. I’ve appended a short cost delta table in the attached proposal (see page 5).

2) p99 behavior / fallbacks: our default behavior is smart routing and graceful degradation — if local capacity is constrained, traffic can failover to a compatible model variant in a different capacity tier or region (if you allow cross-region failover). For strict isolation and PHI, we recommend the following policy: no cross-tenant failover; instead Autoscale reserved burst + queueing with prioritized interactive traffic. Dev — I’ve asked you to confirm the exact failover sequences and how model variants affect output parity.

3) Security artifacts: Dev will send the network topology diagram, SOC 2 export, and audit log retention details. Priya — I’ll set a separate 30-min call for Wed 6/24 with Dev to walk the appendix.

Next immediate step: I’ll have an updated proposal (12 GPU pricing + SLO notes) and a redline-friendly SOW back to you by EOD 6/22. If procurement can confirm their required PO terms, we’ll prep the DocuSign packet.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Priya / Sam —

Attached are the items you asked for:
- Network topology diagram (file: acme_network_topology.png) — shows VPC peering and private control plane options.
- Audit log retention: default retention 90 days; we can configure 12 months for audit logs with an enterprise retention add-on (we’ve noted the configuration steps in the attached doc).
- SOC 2 excerpt: redacted summary + link to full artifact (requires NDA) — I’ll share through the secure portal once we have an access list.

Failover notes: for strict single-tenant Dedicated pools we do NOT automatically fail traffic to multi-tenant hosted pools. Our recommended policy is:
- Primary: Dedicated pool (private, reserved)
- Burst: Reserved burst capacity within the same Dedicated cluster (up to configured +4 GPUs)
- If cluster capacity reached and burst exhausted: queue prioritized interactive requests (short queue with prioritized routing).
- Cross-region failover is available but requires explicit consent due to data locality/PHI considerations.

I’ll be on the call Wed 6/24 10am PT to walk the appendix with Priya.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
